summary_en: Kaihan Co. to acquire Speame Co. via simplified stock exchange, making it a 100% subsidiary effective 2026-08-25. Speame provides marketing support, reservation management, customer support, and consulting services to medical institutions in the medical weight-loss field, generating ~¥300M+ annual gross profit from primary client Kooun Medical Corp. Board approval obtained; Speame shareholders approved at extraordinary meeting. Integration into Kaihan Medical group planned to diversify revenue base in healthcare and expand competitive position.
title_en: Notice regarding full subsidiary acquisition of Speame Co. via simplified stock exchange
translation_en_brief: On 2026-07-15, Kaihan Co. announced it has entered into a stock exchange agreement with Speame Co., making Speame a 100% subsidiary effective 2026-08-25 via simplified stock exchange procedure. Kaihan does not require shareholder approval under the Companies Act § 796(2); Speame obtained approval from an extraordinary shareholder meeting. Speame is a support function provider for Kooun Medical Corp., operating three "Riete Clinic" locations (Nagoya, Tokyo, Yokohama) in the medical weight-loss field. Speame generates ~¥300M+ annual gross profit from primary client services including marketing support, reservation management, customer support, nutritionist services, and management consulting. Kooun Medical reported ~¥2.5B calendar 2025 revenue. Although Speame is in a net debt position due to early-stage losses (2020 founding) and prior client deterioration, the company has specialized expertise and stable operations with Kooun. Kaihan, which previously acquired BOBS and Waiden (merged into Kaihan Medical in Dec 2024), aims to diversify its healthcare revenue base beyond prior key client dependency. Integration with Kaihan Medical is under consideration but deferred pending evaluation of employment systems and business structures. Kaihan views Speame's participation as enabling operational efficiency, service enhancement, and geographic expansion (including Tokyo metropolitan area) toward future nationwide rollout.
